args.title: Add totals row for each currency in XLSX exports
args.body:
File: src/export/

The XLSX export should include a totals row at the bottom of the exported file, summarizing the total amount for each currency present in the report. This will save time for accountants who manually add these sums after export. The CSV export should remain unchanged, as the loaders already handle totals correctly.

args.title: Accept application/octet-stream for .csv files in uploads
args.body:
File: src/routes/uploads.ts

The upload endpoint currently rejects files with `application/octet-stream` content type, even if the file extension is `.csv`. This causes failures for scripts using `curl -F file=@statement.csv`, which sends `application/octet-stream` for unknown extensions. The fix should allow `.csv` files with this content type, matching the behavior of the web form upload.

args.title: Add configurable send time for scheduled exports in report owner's time zone
args.body:
File: src/export/scheduler.ts

Introduce a `sendHourLocal` field in the `Report` schema to allow report owners to specify the hour (in their local time zone) when their scheduled exports should be sent. Modify the `nextRunAt` function to convert this local hour to UTC based on the report owner's time zone, using the time zone stored in the report metadata. This ensures scheduled exports are sent at a time that aligns with the report owner's working hours, addressing the need to include overnight transactions from the West Coast.

args.title: Fix double hyphen in export filenames before the date
args.body:
File: $fill

The issue describes export filenames with a double hyphen (e.g., `--2026-10-21.xlsx`) due to truncation logic that leaves a hyphen when cutting long report names to 60 characters. The fix should ensure that only a single hyphen is added before the date, even if the truncation occurs after a space or comma.

args.title: Add Spanish locale support and translation catalog
args.body:
File: src/i18n/index.ts

1. Extend the `LOCALES` array to include "es" for Spanish.
2. Update the `catalogs` object to import and include a Spanish translation catalog (`es.json`).
3. Ensure the `isLocale` function recognizes "es" as a valid locale.
4. Add a Spanish translation file (`es.json`) in the same directory as the existing language files, containing the translated strings for the application and emails.

This change enables Spanish as a supported language for users in Mexico and Spain, aligning with the request in issue-4337.
